title: Tensor-pullback sections as the étale Hom presheaf
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and F any O_X-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On the small étale category [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the underlying set presheaf U↦Γ(U,tensorPullback(u)F), with the unit-normalized restrictions [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial], is naturally isomorphic to U↦Hom(u^*O_X,u^*F), with the pullHom restrictions of the canonical module-pullback pseudofunctor [def-pc-module-pullback]. Here the latter pullback is Mathlib's abstract left adjoint, canonically identified with the tensor-formula one. F need not be quasi-coherent; no sheaf assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 03DT, proof of Lemma 35.8.1: reinterpretation of sections as maps from the pulled-back structure sheaf; Tag 03DR, equation (35.8.0.1)

proof.text: Use tensorSectionsPullbackComparison, the unit-normalized left-adjoint comparison, and pullbackObjUnitIso to identify pulled-back module maps with maps from O_U to tensorPullback(u)F. Evaluation at one is injective by unit_hom_ext and cancellation of the two isomorphisms. It is surjective: the inverse sends s to pullbackObjUnitIso(u).hom followed by homOfGlobalSection(s), followed by the forward comparison. homOfGlobalSection_app_one and the isomorphism identities prove the inverse equation.

The evaluation maps commute with etale restriction by lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-evaluation-naturality. Convert the proved pointwise bijections to equivalences with Equiv.ofBijective and their Type-valued isomorphisms with Equiv.toIso. NatIso.ofComponents assembles these components using the cited naturality equation. Take the inverse of this natural isomorphism to obtain the required orientation.
